corrective_scope: Responds to the independent audit findings F1-F4 against the Batch 10.4 Third Corrective packaging delivery. No Batch 10.5 work performed. No UI, clipboard, download, backup, restore, Prompt Pack, rendered-image, persistence-write, or external-integration work performed.

findings_addressed.F1: hasBrokenOutputLinkage's first-match .find() relational check (which only inspected an identity once it already had a matching selected Output A, and silently skipped it otherwise) is replaced by hasRelationalIntegrityViolation - a bounded relational index that groups every selected Output A, selected Output B, and numbering row by the complete (sessionId, sceneId) identity before any comparison runs, so >1 selected A, >1 selected B, or >1 numbering row per identity is counted and rejected deterministically, independent of array insertion order (proven directly by a forward-vs-reverse-order test asserting identical failure codes).
findings_addressed.F2: Explicit scope-content-policy categories now drive the relational rules: pair-bearing scopes (pair, group, session, complete_project, all) require exactly one selected A, one selected B, and one numbering row per identity with full ID agreement; B-only scopes (output_b, group_b) require exactly one numbering row consistent with the selected B without requiring a selected A; A-only scopes (output_a, group_a) require exactly one numbering row consistent with each selected A. Every selected output's session/scene must also lie within the plan's resolved scope.
findings_addressed.F3: Pair-file emission (shouldEmitPairFile plus the per-session emission loop) now runs only after hasRelationalIntegrityViolation has already rejected any plan carrying more than one selected A/B/numbering row per identity, and additionally tracks already-emitted (sessionId, sceneId) identities in the emission loop itself (Set-based defense-in-depth) so a single validated identity can never emit more than one collision-suffixed pair file even if the upstream gate regresses.
findings_addressed.F4: The ZIP verifier's local-byte-range coverage pass now walks local entries in the exact order they were populated during central-directory iteration (canonical path order) and never independently sorts them by offset - closing a gap where a byte-reordered but structurally-complete archive (central directory in strict canonical order, every entry individually well-formed) could pass a coverage check that only proved gap-free coverage without checking physical order against declared central order. Adds the local_order_mismatch reason with the required precedence: local_offset_reused -> local_order_mismatch -> local_entry_overlap -> local_entry_gap -> bytes_before_central_directory.
